opening.text: Many of us have written a thank-you note in our heads and never sent it. We meant to. We felt thankful. But life moved on, and the note stayed unwritten.
Gratitude is like that. We feel it, but we do not always say it. I would like to talk about gratitude, and why it matters so much to God.

mainMessage.text: Everything good we have comes from God. He asks us to give thanks, and not just for big things. Gratitude opens our eyes to His gifts. It lifts us in hard times. It draws us closer to the Savior. And it moves us to live better. A thankful heart is a happy one.

blocks.text: Everything we have is from Him.

King Benjamin taught his people that even if they gave all their thanks to God, they would still be in His debt. He creates us, keeps us, and lends us breath every moment. And the Lord commanded us to thank Him in all things.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—I say unto you that if ye should serve him who has created you from the beginning, and is preserving you from day to day, by lending you breath, that ye may live and move and do according to your own will, and even supporting you from one moment to another—I say, if ye should serve him with all your whole souls yet ye would be unprofitable servants.
Thou shalt thank the Lord thy God in all things.
President Gordon B. Hinckley said this. It is printed in Teachings of Gordon B. Hinckley, page 216. It is a book, not a conference talk.
They will mature with a sense of appreciation, having heard their parents in prayer express gratitude for blessings great and small. They will grow with faith in the living God.
Gratitude for small things is still gratitude.
We thank Him most for His Son.
Paul called the Savior God’s unspeakable gift. Alma taught that we should live in thanksgiving daily for the many mercies and blessings God gives us. The greatest of these is the Atonement.
Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.

That ye contend no more against the Holy Ghost, but that ye receive it, and take upon you the name of Christ; that ye humble yourselves even to the dust, and worship God, in whatsoever place ye may be in, in spirit and in truth; and that ye live in thanksgiving daily, for the many mercies and blessings which he doth bestow upon you.
President Thomas S. Monson said this in his talk “At Parting” from the April 2011 general conference.

At the last moment, He could have turned back. But He did not. He passed beneath all things that He might save all things. In doing so, He gave us life beyond this mortal existence. He reclaimed us from the Fall of Adam. To the depths of my very soul, I am grateful to Him. He taught us how to live. He taught us how to die. He secured our salvation.
Our deepest thanks belong to Jesus Christ.
Gratitude grows when we remember.

It is easy to forget what we have received. Nephi’s brother Jacob reminded people to remember the words of God, to pray by day, and to give thanks by night. David told his own soul not to forget all the Lord’s benefits.
Behold, my beloved brethren, remember the words of your God; pray unto him continually by day, and give thanks unto his holy name by night. Let your hearts rejoice.
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “O Remember, Remember” from the October 2007 general conference.

More than gratitude began to grow in my heart. Testimony grew. I became ever more certain that our Heavenly Father hears and answers prayers. I felt more gratitude for the softening and refining that come because of the Atonement of the Savior Jesus Christ. And I grew more confident that the Holy Ghost can bring all things to our remembrance—even things we did not notice or pay attention to when they happened.
When we look for God’s hand, we find it.
We give thanks in every circumstance.
That is harder. Paul said, in every thing give thanks, for this is the will of God. The Lord told the Saints in a hard time to be comforted, to rejoice, and in everything give thanks.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Verily I say unto you my friends, fear not, let your hearts be comforted; yea, rejoice evermore, and in everything give thanks;
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pray Always” from the October 2008 general conference.

We notice during this particular day that there are occasions where normally we would have a tendency to speak harshly, and we do not; or we might be inclined to anger, but we are not. We discern heavenly help and strength and humbly recognize answers to our prayer. Even in that moment of recognition, we offer a silent prayer of gratitude.
Gratitude does not deny the hard parts. It sees the help in them too.
Gratitude brings blessings.

The Lord said that he who receives all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious. Paul taught that all things work together for good for those who love God. Looking back, we often see how true that was.
He who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious; and the things of this earth shall be added unto him, even an hundred fold, yea, more.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Henry B. Eyring of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Education for Real Life” in the October 2002 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Your life is carefully watched over, as was mine. The Lord knows both what He will need you to do and what you will need to know. He is kind and He is all-knowing. So, you can with confidence expect that He has prepared opportunities for you to learn in preparation for the service you will give. You will not recognize those opportunities perfectly, as I did not. But when you put the spiritual things first in your life, you will be blessed to feel directed toward certain learning and you will be motivated to work harder. You will recognize later that your power to serve was increased, and you will be grateful.
Some thanks only comes when we look back.
Gratitude shapes how we live.

Paul told the Colossians to let the peace of God rule in their hearts, and to be thankful. Whatever we do, we do in the name of Jesus Christ, giving thanks. David said to enter His gates with thanksgiving.

And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Divine Gift of Repentance” from the October 2011 general conference.

I gratefully acknowledge and testify that the incomprehensible suffering, death, and Resurrection of our Lord ‘bringeth to pass the condition of repentance’ (Helaman 14:18). The divine gift of repentance is the key to happiness here and hereafter. In the Savior’s words and in deep humility and love, I invite all to ‘repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand’ (Matthew 4:17). I know that in accepting this invitation, you will find joy both now and forever.
A grateful heart wants to follow Him.

story.title: One leper returns to give thanks

blocks.text: Ten men with leprosy cried out to Jesus Christ for mercy. He healed them all. But only one came back.

And it came to pass, as he went to Jerusalem, that he passed through the midst of Samaria and Galilee. And as he entered into a certain village, there met him ten men that were lepers, which stood afar off: And they lifted up their voices, and said, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. And when he saw them, he said unto them, Go shew yourselves unto the priests. And it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed. And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan. And Jesus answering said, Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger. And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.
Nine were healed. One was made whole. Gratitude did something more than a blessing could do. It turned a healed man into a changed man.

story.title: Paul and Silas sing in prison

blocks.text: Paul and Silas had been beaten and put in prison. Their feet were locked in stocks. It was midnight. What did they do?

And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them. And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.
They praised God in the worst place and at the worst hour. Their gratitude was not about the setting. It was about who God is. When we give thanks in dark times, we make room for light.

story.title: Jonah gives thanks from the deep

blocks.text: Jonah ran from God. He ended up in the belly of a great fish, with no way out. And there, he turned back.

When my soul fainted within me I remembered the Lord: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple. They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy. But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the Lord.
Jonah’s thanks came before his rescue. He remembered God, and he gave thanks while he was still in the dark. Gratitude can be the first step back.

The jar has slips from easy days and hard ones. Paul said to give thanks in every thing. The Lord told His Saints to be comforted and to give thanks in everything.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Verily I say unto you my friends, fear not, let your hearts be comforted; yea, rejoice evermore, and in everything give thanks;
Elder David A. Bednar of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pray Always” from the October 2008 general conference.

We notice during this particular day that there are occasions where normally we would have a tendency to speak harshly, and we do not; or we might be inclined to anger, but we are not. We discern heavenly help and strength and humbly recognize answers to our prayer. Even in that moment of recognition, we offer a silent prayer of gratitude.
Hard days hold small mercies. We can write those down too.
What the jar shows at year’s end.
When we read the slips later, we see a pattern. The Lord said the thankful will be made glorious. Paul said all things work together for good to those who love God.
He who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious; and the things of this earth shall be added unto him, even an hundred fold, yea, more.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
Elder Henry B. Eyring of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “Education for Real Life” in the October 2002 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

Your life is carefully watched over, as was mine. The Lord knows both what He will need you to do and what you will need to know. He is kind and He is all-knowing. So, you can with confidence expect that He has prepared opportunities for you to learn in preparation for the service you will give. You will not recognize those opportunities perfectly, as I did not. But when you put the spiritual things first in your life, you will be blessed to feel directed toward certain learning and you will be motivated to work harder. You will recognize later that your power to serve was increased, and you will be grateful.
The pattern shows a God who was paying attention.
Thankful in word and deed.
Gratitude does not stay in a jar. Paul told the Colossians to be thankful and to do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus. David said to enter His gates with thanksgiving.

And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
Elder D. Todd Christofferson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “The Divine Gift of Repentance” from the October 2011 general conference.

I gratefully acknowledge and testify that the incomprehensible suffering, death, and Resurrection of our Lord ‘bringeth to pass the condition of repentance’ (Helaman 14:18). The divine gift of repentance is the key to happiness here and hereafter. In the Savior’s words and in deep humility and love, I invite all to ‘repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand’ (Matthew 4:17). I know that in accepting this invitation, you will find joy both now and forever.
Gratitude moves from the heart to the hands.

story.title: Jesus gives thanks before feeding the multitude

blocks.text: A crowd was hungry. The disciples had five loaves and two small fish. Jesus Christ did something before He fed them.
And Jesus took the loaves; and when he had given thanks, he distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to them that were set down; and likewise of the fishes as much as they would.
He gave thanks first. He did not wait for plenty. He gave thanks for what He had, and it was enough for all. Thanks can turn a little into enough.

application.text: First, start a gratitude jar this week. Add one slip each day. Second, read it aloud with your family on a Sunday. Third, when you receive a little, thank God for it before asking for more.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that God hears our thanks. I know that He gives more than we notice. I know that Jesus Christ gave His life for us, and I am grateful. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to start a gratitude jar this week and add one slip each day.
I invite you to read the slips aloud with your family on Sunday.

closingVerse.text: For as the heaven is high above the earth, so great is his mercy toward them that fear him. As far as the east is from the west, so far hath he removed our transgressions from us. Like as a father pitieth his children, so the Lord pitieth them that fear him.

opening.text: At a well-set table, someone has put in effort. The food is hot. The plates are laid out. Before we eat, many families pause and give thanks. That pause is small, but it says something. It says we know where the meal came from.
I would like to talk about that pause, and about living with a thankful heart.

mainMessage.text: God is the giver of all we have. He asks for our thanks, and He gave His Son for us. When we remember, we grow. When we give thanks in trials, we find help. And over time, gratitude shapes the way we live and serve.

blocks.text: Someone prepared the table.
King Benjamin taught that God made us, keeps us alive, and supports us each moment. We can never repay Him. Still, the Lord asks us to thank Him in all things.

I say unto you, my brethren, that if you should render all the thanks and praise which your whole soul has power to possess, to that God who has created you, and has kept and preserved you, and has caused that ye should rejoice, and has granted that ye should live in peace one with another—I say unto you that if ye should serve him who has created you from the beginning, and is preserving you from day to day, by lending you breath, that ye may live and move and do according to your own will, and even supporting you from one moment to another—I say, if ye should serve him with all your whole souls yet ye would be unprofitable servants.
Thou shalt thank the Lord thy God in all things.
President Gordon B. Hinckley said this. It is printed in Teachings of Gordon B. Hinckley, page 216. It is a book, not a conference talk.
They will mature with a sense of appreciation, having heard their parents in prayer express gratitude for blessings great and small. They will grow with faith in the living God.
A thankful home grows thankful people.
The costliest part of the meal.
The best gift came at the highest price. Paul called it unspeakable. Alma asked us to live in thanksgiving daily for God’s mercies and blessings.
Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.

That ye contend no more against the Holy Ghost, but that ye receive it, and take upon you the name of Christ; that ye humble yourselves even to the dust, and worship God, in whatsoever place ye may be in, in spirit and in truth; and that ye live in thanksgiving daily, for the many mercies and blessings which he doth bestow upon you.
President Thomas S. Monson said this in his talk “At Parting” from the April 2011 general conference.

At the last moment, He could have turned back. But He did not. He passed beneath all things that He might save all things. In doing so, He gave us life beyond this mortal existence. He reclaimed us from the Fall of Adam. To the depths of my very soul, I am grateful to Him. He taught us how to live. He taught us how to die. He secured our salvation.
He paid it in full. Our thanks is the least we can offer.
Pause and remember.
A blessing at the table is a way of remembering. Jacob asked us to give thanks to God each night. David told his soul not to forget His benefits.
Behold, my beloved brethren, remember the words of your God; pray unto him continually by day, and give thanks unto his holy name by night. Let your hearts rejoice.
Bless the Lord, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “O Remember, Remember” from the October 2007 general conference.

More than gratitude began to grow in my heart. Testimony grew. I became ever more certain that our Heavenly Father hears and answers prayers. I felt more gratitude for the softening and refining that come because of the Atonement of the Savior Jesus Christ. And I grew more confident that the Holy Ghost can bring all things to our remembrance—even things we did not notice or pay attention to when they happened.
A small pause can grow a large faith.
Thanks when the table is bare.
Some seasons are lean. The scriptures still call us to give thanks. Paul said in every thing give thanks. The Lord told His friends to be comforted, and in everything give thanks.
In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
Verily I say unto you my friends, fear not, let your hearts be comforted; yea, rejoice evermore, and in everything give thanks;

We discern heavenly help and strength and humbly recognize answers to our prayer. Even in that moment of recognition, we offer a silent prayer of gratitude.
Help is often there before we see it.
Why the meal was prepared.
The Lord said the thankful will be made glorious. Paul said all things work together for good to those who love God. We may not see the full picture today. We often do later.
He who receiveth all things with thankfulness shall be made glorious; and the things of this earth shall be added unto him, even an hundred fold, yea, more.
And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.

You will not recognize those opportunities perfectly, as I did not. But when you put the spiritual things first in your life, you will be blessed to feel directed toward certain learning and you will be motivated to work harder. You will recognize later that your power to serve was increased, and you will be grateful.
One day we may see the whole table, and say thank you.
Leave the table changed.
Gratitude should send us out better than we came in. Paul told the Colossians to be thankful and to do all in the name of the Lord Jesus. David said to enter His gates with thanksgiving.

And let the peace of God rule in your hearts, to the which also ye are called in one body; and be ye thankful. Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. story.prompt: The member tells a true time about feeling grateful to God. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Lehi’s family gives thanks

blocks.text: Lehi’s sons had gone back to Jerusalem for the brass plates. Their mother, Sariah, feared they were lost. Then they returned.

And it came to pass that after they had given thanks unto the God of Israel, my father, Lehi, took the records which were engraven upon the plates of brass, and he did search them from the beginning. And he beheld that they did contain the five books of Moses, which gave an account of the creation of the world, and also of Adam and Eve, which were our first parents;
First, they gave thanks. Then they searched the scriptures. Gratitude came before the next step. It prepared their hearts to learn.

application.text: First, pause before one meal each day and give a sincere thanks. Make it specific. Second, write a short note of thanks to God, listing what you have received this month. Third, look for one person to serve this week, as a way to show your thanks.
